I maintain if you don't learn how to properly defend yourself then you are setting yourself up to be taken advantage of.

So learn a method of self defense/martial art.

I would recommend one that deals with weapons as well (krav maga, FMA/silat/escrima) because we live in the real world and people carry weapons.

If you have no options as such nearby pick a martial art and make sure the school is reputable and a good teacher. (Usually if they have a tournament team or regularly participate in competitions then it's a decent school)

There are a lot of martial arts schools where the focus is the art ( patterns, traditionalism) and there are others that do sport and competition. The sport and competition allows you to spar and pressure test, so you get actively used to what works for you and what doesn't, as well as becoming more relaxed on stressful situations. I do a fair share of martial arts. Nearly half of every week I spend on training weapons ( knives, sticks, etc.).

Tldr: Learn self defense. Make sure place does FULL contact sparring. Make sure place does sport/competition if a more traditional art (judo, tkd, karate, etc.)

Martial arts are great when you're young to learn control and the basic concepts of fighting. When you get older they help you stay in shape. Good stuff, but taking it to seriously and thinking you can disarm a robber well just get you shot.

The value of what you will learn will very strongly depend on the school. Most traditional martial arts won't be very good in a fight unless the school is teaching you with the intention of you using it in a real fight and not a tournament. To that end, I'd advise avoiding aikido, ju jitsu and tae kwon do schools. As others have said, the Okinawa styles tend to be more complete. Some hints: there is no blocking, there is redirecting and dodging. Most kata and most stances are about teaching you a concept and building muscles. In a real fight, I'd find it very unlikely to be using a horse stance but having the muscles to do a horse stance for ten minutes means I can kick my opponent in the face tirelessly.
